title: I AM THE LORD — THE PROMISE SEALED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""And I will bring you to the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob. I will give it to you as a possession. I am the Lord.'"" - Exodus 6:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God ends this string of promises the way He began it: I am the Lord. The promises are wrapped in His name like a seal on a document.

That is what guarantees them. Not Israel's worthiness — they had none to offer. Not favourable circumstances — those were terrible. Only God's own character stands behind His word.

The phrase "with uplifted hand" pictures a solemn oath. God, in a sense, swore by Himself, because there is no one greater to swear by. Hebrews makes exactly this point: God confirmed His promise with an oath so that we might be greatly encouraged (Heb 6:17-18).

Be careful not to lift the specific land promise out of its covenant setting and apply it to your own hopes. That was said to Israel, about Canaan.

What is genuinely ours is the same unshakeable foundation. Everything God has promised us in Christ rests not on our performance but on who He is. If God's name is on it, it will happen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I trusting God's promises because of my performance or because of His name?
2. What would change today if I truly believed God cannot break His word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You have staked Your own name on Your promises. Teach me to rest in Your faithfulness rather than my feelings. Amen.
